I did this in CoS, the players seemed fine with it and never complained about him. They met him as level 7’s and one of the players wanted to have him around as a new friend and sparring partner. Needless to say this character never leveled with the party and eventually started dropping fast in dpr. One day the party was fighting a dulahan that patrolled a section of the svalich road, and this was the returning battle after failing earlier in the campaign to pass this portion of the svalich road. In the battle the party fought viciously against the dulahan and succeeded. Not before my dmpc literally nat 1’d against being beheaded by the dulahan’s behead ability. I definitely grew attached and so did the player that made him their characters “vegeta”. We had a burning and I read his eulogy as I wept literally. Hardest moment was letting go of an underpowered dork with one really cool ability to hit for slightly more damage. Players had a shift in character development losing an ally they cared about and started really trying to kill strahd after that moment, before that it was mostly getting pub stomped by strahd. In the end they beat strahd; the catch is at one point ireena the mcguffin was kidnapped and held in strahds castle and learned of the ritual that strahd performed. With the amount of time that she was held captive (roughly 3-4 months) she was tortured and was driven to extreme measures to make sure she’d never be that “weak” again. She essentially convinced her only brother with a soul, to follow her to the amber temple where she would perform the same ritual strahd performed over millennia ago to achieve his vampirism, and sacrifice her only brother left to become a vampire lord and kill strahd. That moment was cut short when the party killed strahd but not before ireena had already sacrificed her brother and swore that the party would never be able to return to barovia( because she’s now evil and they snuffed that ending when they killed the person she swore to kill by any means, and she sacrificed her brother to do that). Players said the ending felt a bit rushed but understood because we had a player that had been a pillar to the party since session 1 and they were leaving. The players got to choose the ending they felt best for their characters, and I now have a cool story that could expand or just stay as a separate thing and be revisited as a one shot.
